record.original_question: Let N_0 be an index-2 subfactor of an ultrapower N^U. Must N_0 be isomorphic to an ultraproduct ∏_{i→U} N_i where each N_i ⊂ N is an index-2 subfactor?

evidence.quote: Problem 38. Let N0 be an index 2 subfactor of an ultrapower NU. Then is N0 ∼= ∏ i→U Ni where Ni ⊂ N are index 2 subfactors?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $N$ be a separable $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor with normalized trace $\tau$, and let $\mathcal U$ be a free ultrafilter on $\mathbb N$. Form the tracial ultrapower $N^{\mathcal U}$, defined as $\ell^\infty(\mathbb N,N)/\mathcal I_{\mathcal U}$, where $\mathcal I_{\mathcal U}=\{(x_n)\in\ell^\infty(\mathbb N,N):\lim_{n\to\mathcal U}\tau(x_n^*x_n)=0\}$; this is again a $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor. Recall that for an inclusion $A\subset B$ of $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors, the Jones index $[B:A]$ is defined via the coupling constant of the standard representation; an inclusion is said to be of index $2$ when $[B:A]=2$.

Suppose $N_0\subset N^{\mathcal U}$ is a subfactor of index $2$. Must there exist a sequence of index-$2$ subfactors $N_i\subset N$ such that
$$N_0 \;\cong\; \prod_{i\to\mathcal U} N_i$$
as subfactors of $N^{\mathcal U}$ (where the right-hand side denotes the tracial ultraproduct of the inclusions $N_i\subset N$)?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed in a recent (2025) compilation of fifty open problems on ultraproduct II_1 factors as Problem 38. A web search did not surface any published resolution of this specific question concerning whether every index-2 subfactor of an ultrapower II_1 factor arises as an ultraproduct of index-2 subfactors. It therefore appears to remain open.
